referent_label: Trajanic province north of the Danube
note: The province Trajan made in 106. Ptolemy's book and chapter are the locator; the chapter has not been read against a witness for this corpus.

referent_label: Dacia Aureliana south of the Danube
note: After Aurelian withdrew, the name was carried south of the Danube and applied to a new province. Eutropius narrates the act, which is what this row records; the Notitia attests the name in official use a century later and is cited by nmu-dacia-diocese instead.

locator: The map carries no folio or sheet division; the single membrane is the maximum precision available
note: Medieval Latin writers used Dacia for Denmark, and the Hereford map is one witness to the usage. This is the coincidence the trench exists to adjudicate.

A use nobody needed to write down for it to be real: the Dominican province of Dacia covered Denmark, Sweden and Norway from its erection in 1228 until the Reformation dissolved it. Gallen's monograph is the anchor; the page has not been read, so the locator is still pending.

referent_label: The ancient province restored on a modern sheet
note: Ortelius restores the ancient province in the historical supplement to the Theatrum. The sheet is named; the impression has not been examined.

Dacia as an identity claim rather than a territory. Left deliberately low-confidence and open-ended: Trench F is where this is argued, and this row exists so the essay can point at it without absorbing it.
A station on the road to Porolissum.

institution: Consiliul de Stat al Republicii Socialiste Romania
note: Re-attached by decree in 1974. The instrument is administrative, and it is the whole reason the name is there. The decree is now cited; which article carries the renaming has not been read, so the locator is still pending.

referent_label: Dioecesis Daciae, the civil diocese south of the Danube
note: A different administrative level from the province of the same name, and the clearest case that the referent is not the word: one Dacia contains the other, and neither is Trajan's.

referent_label: DACIA as a personification struck on imperial coinage
locator: Reverse types legended DACIA and DACIA FELIX
note: The state naming its own province on the money, which is the use with the widest circulation and the shortest text. No specimen has been examined and no volume or catalogue number is transcribed.
